title: Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick 称 GTA VI 仍需「大力营销」，尽管品牌已全球知名
content:
Strauss Zelnick says GTA VI needs to be 'marketed aggressively'
Marketing
Console
Business
News
Take-Two CEO Strauss Zelnick says GTA VI needs to be 'marketed aggressively' despite global brand awareness
Take-Two Interactive CEO Strauss Zelnick says 'we cannot convince people something that something that's bad is good.'
Diego Argüello
,
Contributing Editor, News
,
GameDeveloper.com
September 17, 2026
schedule
2 Min Read
Image via Rockstar Games
Strauss Zelnick, CEO of Rockstar Games parent company Take-Two Interactive, says that
Grand Theft Auto VI
still needs to be "marketed aggressively" despite global brand awareness.
The statement comes from an
interview with GamesBeat
, which took place in a fireside chat at the GamesBeat Insider event yesterday. The CEO used the Barbie movie as an example of a big, recognizable property tie-in that still had a robust marketing campaign behind it, despite the brand familiarity.
"You always have to go out and create enthusiasm," Zelnick says. "So, awareness is one thing; enthusiasm is another thing. And we have to show people what they're going to get because, in linear entertainment, you sit there; it's presented to you. You don't have to interact with it. You don't have to install it. You don't have to have any expertise. You may like it, you may not like it, but it is a lean-back experience."
Related:
Twitch will sacrifice you to its AI overlord whether you like it or not
Zelnick notes that marketing times is similar to TV and movie marketing to a point, in the sense that everyone strives for positive reviews and fan excitement. Games, however, can also be elevated by creators with long-following audiences. But there are limits to this.
"You're amplifying word of mouth because what you can't do is pay anyone to say something that's terrible is good," Zelnick says. "Even if they're the most craven creator on earth, the minute they did that, they lose their own audience, right? So, no one's going to do that."
The CEO adds that you can ask a creator to exclusively play a game for a couple days, and reward said promotion. Yet, he emphasizes that you can't game the system.
"We cannot convince people something that something that's bad is good. What we can do is say to people, 'Look, it's out there. You're being exposed to it. It's important. You ought to try it."
Zelnick's comments regarding the strategy and culture at the company comes at a time in which Rockstar is undergoing an
union busting tribunal
in the UK. This has been the culmination of
Rockstar firing 34 workers
(31 union members and three non-members) across the UK and Canada last year, over what the studio claimed as gross misconduct related to the
leaking of confidential information
. Those impacted, however, alleged they were dismissed for engaging in trade union activity.
GamesBeat didn't raise the topic with Zelnick during the Q&A.
The legal drama and highly-anticipated launch of
GTA VI
have led to an exceptional amount of interest in the company's goals and financial future. For his part, Zelnick says the company's mission is to make the "best entertainment on earth," which remains its focus to this day.
Related:
Rockstar wants you to pay Netflix to watch the next GTA VI trailer before it's released to the masses
"We have a mission statement and a strategy and a culture. It’s all stated. We have to state it here. We say it every time we talk internally, and it starts with trying to make the biggest and best hits."
